purpose.assets: Embedded HTML template and language icon assets used by renderers to produce the browser-facing output.
purpose.cmd/stacklit: Thin CLI executable entrypoint that delegates command handling to internal/cli.
purpose.internal/archexport: Transforms a Stacklit index into the architecture-export interchange document.
purpose.internal/cli: Cobra-style command layer for stacklit workflows including indexing, rendering, diffs, insights, derive output, and exit-code mapping.
purpose.internal/config: Project configuration loader and defaults for ignore rules, scan limits, and output paths.
purpose.internal/derive: Utilities that turn a schema index into compact injectable summaries and update target files with generated blocks.
purpose.internal/detect: Heuristics for detecting frameworks, environment variables, and repository conventions from files and imports.
purpose.internal/engine: Central orchestration layer that scans repositories, parses files, builds graphs, applies insights, and writes outputs.
purpose.internal/git: Git-derived activity and content identity helpers, including recent/hot file analysis and Merkle hashing.
purpose.internal/graph: Module dependency graph builder that groups parsed files, computes edges, entrypoints, isolated modules, and dependency rankings.
purpose.internal/hint: Derives actionable feature-placement guidance from indexed modules and entrypoints.
purpose.internal/insights: Load, merge, seed, apply, and write stacklit-insights.json purpose, hint, and architecture overlays.
purpose.internal/jsonfile: Shared JSON marshal and indented write helpers for stable formatted output files.
purpose.internal/monorepo: Repository workspace detector for monorepo tools and workspace layouts.
purpose.internal/parser: Language-aware source parsers that extract imports, exports, type definitions, line counts, and entrypoint flags.
purpose.internal/purpose: Supplies mechanical fallback module-purpose text when curated insight is unavailable.
purpose.internal/renderer: JSON, Markdown, Mermaid, and HTML output generation from the canonical schema index.
purpose.internal/schema: Canonical data model for project indexes, module metadata, dependencies, git activity, hints, and multi-repo summaries.
purpose.internal/summary: AI-assisted summary command integration that generates insights files from schema indexes.
purpose.internal/walker: Filesystem traversal with ignore handling to produce the source file list for indexing.
purpose.root: Shell installer and convenience indexing scripts outside the Go application packages.

hints.add_feature: For new CLI-visible behavior, start in internal/cli, delegate orchestration to internal/engine, add schema fields in internal/schema only when the output contract changes, and update renderer/insights handling for any new index data.

architecture.ai_summary:
Stacklit is a CLI that turns a repository into a committed JSON index for AI agents. README.md explains this fork's CLI-only surface; USAGE.md covers commands, configuration and refresh workflows. generate-json passes options to engine.Run, which loads .stacklitrc.json and resolves the parse-worker count: the CLI flag overrides config, the default is 3, and values below 1 fail before scanning. Run then detects workspaces, walks gitignore-aware sources (configured Stacklit outputs are excluded so they never feed back), parses files and builds the module graph. It adds Git activity and framework and env-var metadata, computes a Merkle fingerprint (a hash over walked paths and contents), applies stacklit-insights.json and writes stacklit.json. The query, derive, view and export-architecture commands only read that saved snapshot, so edited insights reach readers only after regeneration (internal/engine/engine.go).

Parsing emits one FileInfo record per file: Go through its standard AST, ten other languages through per-call Tree-sitter state, and a generic fallback for the rest. ParseAllWithWorkers bounds concurrency, restores input order and collects per-file errors without aborting. Graph assembly stays sequential, so output determinism depends on that ordering (internal/parser/parser.go). Graph building skips test and fixture directories and applies depth and module caps; index assembly then drops references to modules it did not keep. Extraction changes stay local as long as FileInfo semantics hold. Changing module identity or index fields needs coordinated edits across graph, schema, renderer, derive, insights and archexport.

Failure handling is deliberately asymmetric. Missing Git data, monorepo detection errors and individual parse failures degrade without stopping the scan; malformed insights, invalid worker counts and write errors abort. RunMulti scans repos one after another: worker-count errors abort it, while other scan failures print a warning and skip that repo. stacklit diff recomputes the Merkle hash and exits 0 when current, 1 when sources changed, 2 on failure. It detects source drift, not stale insights (internal/cli/diff.go). The JSON writer keeps GeneratedAt when content is semantically unchanged and skips byte-identical writes, which keeps commits of the index quiet.

Semantic enrichment has its own lifecycle. init-insights seeds missing entries. ai-summary runs one local agent (claude -p by default, overridable with STACKLIT_SUMMARY_CMD, timeout from STACKLIT_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT) on ranked documentation excerpts plus a snapshot, then Stacklit merges the result. Generated purposes and add_feature hints replace only mechanically inferred values, custom test commands are kept, the summary is replaced, and stale purposes, do_not_touch paths and env_vars are pruned. When insights are applied, exact purpose keys win over basename keys. Drafting before reconciling is required by the prompt but not enforced by file isolation. The direct Anthropic API path in summary.Generate is not wired to the CLI (internal/cli/insights.go, internal/insights/insights.go, internal/summary/).

Implementations must build with Go 1.25.0 (go.mod), keep the MIT notices (LICENSE) and stay within the CLI-only surface README.md defines; GUARDRAILS.md adds no product rules yet. specs/map-reduce.md requires parsing changes to preserve schema and graph semantics. The drafts under specs/arch-plan and specs/plans predate the current default of 3 workers, so treat them as history; specs/benchmarks/map-reduce/benchmark-report.md has the latency and memory evidence. Worker counts bound concurrent parses, not total memory, because the engine later reads and keeps every file's contents for hashing. Use the purpose and hints fields and stacklit derive for navigation; this summary adds runtime sequencing, failure boundaries and which contracts must change together.
